from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        robot = Triangle(color=GOLD).scale(0.12).move_to(dot_pos).rotate(-PI/2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup lines and layout
        title = "The 'i' Operator: Rotation, Not Just a Number"
        lines = [
            "Multiplying by i isn't just scaling; it's rotating.",
            "One multiplication by i pivots 90 degrees counter-clockwise.",
            "Starting at one, we land on the imaginary unit.",
            "Multiplying by i again rotates another 90 degrees.",
            "Two rotations land us exactly at negative one."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Reference points for the complex plane
        # Origin at D3, '1' at D4, 'i' at C3, '-1' at D2
        origin_point = self.grid["D3"]
        pos_1 = self.grid["D4"]
        pos_i = self.grid["C3"]
        pos_minus_1 = self.grid["D2"]

        # Simple coordinate axes
        xaxis = Line(self.grid["D1"], self.grid["D5"], color=GRAY_B)
        yaxis = Line(self.grid["F3"], self.grid["B3"], color=GRAY_B)
        axes = VGroup(xaxis, yaxis)

        # Digit the Robot representation (Asset: Robot/robot.png - using a styled placeholder)
        # We will represent the robot with a blue circle and a face to show orientation
        robot = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=0.3, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.8),
            Dot(radius=0.04, color=WHITE).shift(UP*0.1 + RIGHT*0.1), # Right eye
            Dot(radius=0.04, color=WHITE).shift(DOWN*0.1 + RIGHT*0.1), # Left eye
            Line(LEFT*0.15, RIGHT*0.15, color=WHITE).shift(DOWN*0.0) # Simple face feature
        )
        # Note: Robot faces RIGHT initially
        robot.move_to(pos_1)

        # Labels
        label_1 = Text("1", font_size=20).next_to(pos_1, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        label_i = Text("i", font_size=20, color="#00FF00").next_to(pos_i, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        label_minus_1 = Text("-1", font_size=20, color="#FF0000").next_to(pos_minus_1, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.play(FadeIn(robot), Write(label_1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Arc for rotation (90 degrees CCW)
        arc1 = ArcBetweenPoints(pos_1, pos_i, radius=1.0, color="#00FF00")
        
        # Rotation animation: pivot robot around origin
        self.play(
            Rotate(robot, angle=PI/2, about_point=origin_point, rate_func=smooth),
            Create(arc1),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(Write(label_i))
        self.play(Flash(label_i, color="#00FF00", flash_radius=0.3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Second Arc (90 degrees CCW)
        arc2 = ArcBetweenPoints(pos_i, pos_minus_1, radius=1.0, color="#00FF00")
        
        self.play(
            Rotate(robot, angle=PI/2, about_point=origin_point, rate_func=smooth),
            Create(arc2),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(Write(label_minus_1))
        self.play(Indicate(label_minus_1, color="#FF0000"))
        self.wait(2)

        # Cleanup highlight
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Group Theory Lens: Symmetry and SO(2)", 
            [
                "All unit rotations form the group called U(1).", 
                "Addition in exponents maps to multiplication on the circle.", 
                "Group theory views this formula as a symmetry map."
            ]
        )
        
        # Colors
        GREY_CIRCLE = "#888888"
        LIGHT_BLUE = "#ADD8E6"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = YELLOW
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # 1. Fade in a unit circle in grey
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=GREY_CIRCLE)
        self.place_in_area(circle, 'B2', 'E5')
        center = circle.get_center()
        
        # To show rotation, add a radius line and a dot
        radius_line = Line(center, circle.point_at_angle(0), color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        rotation_dot = Dot(circle.point_at_angle(0), color=WHITE, radius=0.05)
        
        group_visual = VGroup(circle, radius_line, rotation_dot)
        
        # 3. Display text 'Group SO(2)'
        so2_label = Text("Group SO(2)", color=LIGHT_BLUE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(so2_label, 'A3', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(circle),
            FadeIn(so2_label),
            FadeIn(radius_line),
            FadeIn(rotation_dot)
        )
        
        # 2. Show a rotation animation (continuous group action)
        rotation_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def update_group(m):
            angle = rotation_tracker.get_value()
            target_point = circle.point_at_angle(angle)
            m[1].put_start_and_end_on(center, target_point)
            m[2].move_to(target_point)
            
        group_visual.add_updater(update_group)
        
        self.play(rotation_tracker.animate.set_value(2 * PI), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # 4. Draw a mapping arrow from the Real number line
        real_line = NumberLine(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            length=3,
            color=WHITE,
            include_numbers=True,
            font_size=18,
            label_constructor=Text
        )
        self.place_at_grid(real_line, 'F3')
        real_label = Text("Real Numbers (Additive)", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(real_label, 'F5')
        
        # Stop continuous rotation for demonstration
        group_visual.remove_updater(update_group)
        
        # Arrow from number line to circle
        map_arrow = CurvedArrow(
            real_line.n2p(1), 
            circle.point_at_angle(1), 
            angle=-PI/2, 
            color=YELLOW,
            tip_length=0.15
        )
        
        self.play(Create(real_line), FadeIn(real_label))
        self.play(Create(map_arrow))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # 5. Highlight addition of two angles
        theta1 = 1.0
        theta2 = 0.8
        
        arc1 = Arc(radius=1.5, start_angle=0, angle=theta1, color=BLUE, arc_center=center)
        arc2 = Arc(radius=1.5, start_angle=theta1, angle=theta2, color=GREEN, arc_center=center)
        
        self.play(Create(arc1))
        self.play(Create(arc2))
        
        formula_text = Text("exp(ia) * exp(ib) = exp(i(a+b))", font_size=18, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(formula_text, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        symmetry_text = Text("Symmetry: Rotation Transformation", font_size=18, color=LIGHT_BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(symmetry_text, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(arc1), FadeOut(arc2), FadeOut(map_arrow), FadeOut(formula_text),
            FadeIn(symmetry_text)
        )
        
        # Resume rotation using the dot/line to represent symmetry in action
        group_visual.add_updater(update_group)
        self.play(rotation_tracker.animate.set_value(4 * PI), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Exponential Path: Compounding Rotations", 
            [
                'Base e represents a process of continuous growth.', 
                'In e to the ix, growth is always perpendicular.', 
                'Perpendicular growth forces movement along a circular arc.', 
                'Imagine thousands of tiny, compounding right-angle turns.', 
                'This sequence converges into a perfect unit circle.'
            ]
        )
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_RADIUS = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_GROWTH = "#00FFFF"
        
        # Center point for the circle
        center_point = self.grid["D3"]
        unit_length = 1.5

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a vector from the origin to (1,0) in white
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_RADIUS)
        radius_vec = Vector([unit_length, 0, 0], color=COLOR_RADIUS)
        radius_vec.shift(center_point)
        
        self.play(Create(radius_vec))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Draw a small velocity vector at (1,0) pointing exactly perpendicular (upwards) in cyan
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_GROWTH)
        vel_vec = Arrow(
            start=radius_vec.get_end(), 
            end=radius_vec.get_end() + UP * 0.8, 
            color=COLOR_GROWTH,
            buff=0
        )
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(vel_vec))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show movement along a circular arc
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_GROWTH)
        
        theta_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Persistent objects
        def update_radius(m):
            angle = theta_tracker.get_value()
            new_end = center_point + np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0]) * unit_length
            m.put_start_and_end_on(center_point, new_end)

        def update_vel(m):
            angle = theta_tracker.get_value()
            tip_pos = center_point + np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0]) * unit_length
            perp_dir = np.array([-np.sin(angle), np.cos(angle), 0])
            m.put_start_and_end_on(tip_pos, tip_pos + perp_dir * 0.8)

        # Trace the path
        path = TracedPath(radius_vec.get_end, stroke_color=COLOR_GROWTH, stroke_width=4)
        self.add(path)
        
        radius_vec.add_updater(update_radius)
        vel_vec.add_updater(update_vel)
        
        self.play(theta_tracker.animate.set_value(PI / 2), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Imagine thousands of tiny, compounding right-angle turns.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_GROWTH)
        
        # To visualize "steps", we can show the path being built by segments
        # But for smooth animation flow, we continue the rotation with an effect
        # We will rotate further to 3*PI/2 to show the compounding
        self.play(theta_tracker.animate.set_value(3 * PI / 2), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This sequence converges into a perfect unit circle.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_RADIUS)
        
        # Complete the circle
        self.play(theta_tracker.animate.set_value(2 * PI), run_time=1.5, rate_func=linear)
        
        # Label the path
        label = Text("Continuous Perpendicular Growth", font_size=20, color=COLOR_RADIUS)
        self.place_at_grid(label, "B5")
        
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.wait(2)

        # Clean up updaters
        radius_vec.remove_updater(update_radius)
        vel_vec.remove_updater(update_vel)

class Section5Scene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # Background and Title
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        # Left-side lecture content
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        self.lecture.scale(0.85).to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5)
        
        # Fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Mapping grid to the right side of the screen
                x = 1.0 + j * 0.9
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.9
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def construct(self):
        # Configuration and initialization
        title_string = "Group Theory: The Visual Harmony of Euler's Identity"
        lecture_items = [
            "- Rotation as a Group Operation",
            "- The Unit Circle in the Complex Plane",
            "- Mapping SO(2) to Complex Numbers",
            "- Geometric Interpretation of e^iπ"
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_string, lecture_items)
        
        # Add Title and Lecture notes
        self.add(self.title)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture, shift=RIGHT))
        
        # Mathematical Visualization on the Grid
        # Use grid points C3 as the center for a complex plane representation
        plane_center = self.grid["C3"]
        plane = ComplexPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        ).move_to(plane_center + RIGHT * 0.5)
        
        circle = Circle(radius=plane.get_x_unit_size(), color=BLUE_B)
        circle.move_to(plane.get_center())
        
        # Vector representing the rotation
        start_point = plane.n2p(1 + 0j)
        end_point = plane.n2p(-1 + 0j)
        
        pointer = Dot(start_point, color=YELLOW)
        label_start = Text("1", font_size=24).next_to(start_point, UR, buff=0.1)
        label_end = Text("-1", font_size=24).next_to(end_point, UL, buff=0.1)
        
        # Path for rotation (e^it)
        arc_path = Arc(
            radius=plane.get_x_unit_size(),
            start_angle=0,
            angle=PI,
            color=YELLOW,
            arc_center=plane.get_center()
        )
        
        # Animation sequence
        self.play(Create(plane), Create(circle))
        self.play(FadeIn(pointer), Write(label_start))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Show the rotation from 1 to -1
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(pointer, arc_path),
            Create(arc_path),
            run_time=2.5,
            rate_func=smooth
        )
        self.play(Write(label_end))
        
        # Final formula display
        # Use Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependency error
        formula = Text("e^iπ = -1", color=YELLOW, font_size=42)
        formula.move_to(self.grid["F3"] + RIGHT * 0.5)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        
        self.wait(3)

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Summary: The Bridge Between Algebra and Geometry", 
            [
                "Euler's identity bridges calculus, geometry, and group theory.", 
                "Rotation and growth are two sides of one coin.", 
                "Mathematics finds balance in this single, elegant expression."
            ]
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color match: Yellow
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create Complex Plane elements
        plane = ComplexPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1], 
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1], 
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.2}
        )
        unit_circle = Circle(radius=1, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=2)
        
        # Key Points
        dot_1 = Dot(plane.n2p(1), color=WHITE)
        dot_i = Dot(plane.n2p(1j), color=WHITE)
        dot_m1 = Dot(plane.n2p(-1), color=WHITE)
        
        # Fixed: Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        label_1 = Text("1", font_size=20).next_to(dot_1, DR, buff=0.1)
        label_i = Text("i", font_size=20, slant=ITALIC).next_to(dot_i, UR, buff=0.1)
        label_m1 = Text("-1", font_size=20).next_to(dot_m1, DL, buff=0.1)
        
        # Visual Anchor for the whole complex plane system
        plane_group = VGroup(plane, unit_circle, dot_1, dot_i, dot_m1, label_1, label_i, label_m1)
        self.place_in_area(plane_group, "A1", "E6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Animation 1: Zoom out effect (scale from small)
        plane_group.save_state()
        plane_group.scale(0.1)
        # Fixed: Changed set_alpha to set_opacity for Manim CE v0.19.0 best practices
        plane_group.set_opacity(0)
        self.play(
            plane_group.animate.scale(10).set_opacity(1),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=smooth
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Color match: Teal (Standard Manim replacement for Cyan)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(TEAL)
        
        # Highlights for symmetry: circular path and real axis segment
        p_ref = plane_group[0]
        
        # Rotation path (arc from 1 to -1)
        rotation_path = Arc(
            radius=p_ref.x_axis.get_unit_size(), 
            start_angle=0, 
            angle=PI, 
            color=TEAL, 
            stroke_width=6
        ).move_to(p_ref.n2p(0), aligned_edge=ORIGIN)
        
        # Growth path (linear segment from 1 to -1 on real axis)
        growth_path = Line(
            p_ref.n2p(1), 
            p_ref.n2p(-1), 
            color=TEAL, 
            stroke_width=6
        ).set_stroke(opacity=0.6)
        
        self.play(
            Create(rotation_path),
            Create(growth_path),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Color match: Gold (#FFD700)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        
        # Unified Formula - Fixed: Replaced MathTex with Text
        formula = Text("e^πi + 1 = 0", color="#FFD700", font_size=42)
        # Position at the bottom of the right side grid (Row F)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "F1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(formula, shift=UP), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(Indicate(formula, color="#FFD700", scale_factor=1.1), run_time=1.5)
        
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Visual Harmony of e^(πi) = -1: A Group Theory Perspective
outline.target_audience: University students (Undergraduate Math/Physics) or Advanced High School students

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Complex Plane as a Map
sections.content: Introduce the complex plane where the x-axis represents Real numbers and the y-axis represents Imaginary numbers (i). Establish the 'Unit Circle' as the track where the magic happens.
sections.example: Visualize 'Digit the Robot' standing at the point (1, 0) on a giant 2D grid. The grid isn't just a map; it's a field of transformations.

sections.title: The 'i' Operator: Rotation, Not Just a Number
sections.content: Define multiplying by 'i' as a 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation. Explain that applying 'i' twice (i * i) results in a 180-degree turn to -1.
sections.example: Show Digit the Robot facing right at '1'. Multiplying by 'i' makes him pivot 90 degrees to face 'i' on the vertical axis. Another 'i' turn lands him at '-1'.

sections.title: The Group Theory Lens: Symmetry and SO(2)
sections.content: Introduce the idea of a 'Rotation Group'. In Group Theory, the set of all rotations around a circle forms a continuous group. Euler’s formula is essentially a map from the additive group of Real numbers to the multiplicative group of the Unit Circle.
sections.example: Think of a rotating wheel (The Circle Group U(1)). Every point on the edge represents a state. Adding angles together is the group operation.

sections.title: The Exponential Path: Compounding Rotations
sections.content: Explain that 'e' represents continuous growth. In the context of e^(ix), the 'growth' is perpendicular to the current position, which creates a curve. Using the limit definition of e, we see a sequence of tiny rotations compounding into a circular arc.
sections.example: Imagine Digit the Robot taking 1,000 tiny steps, each slightly 'leftward' (perpendicular) to his path. Instead of growing outward, he is forced to walk in a perfect circle.

sections.title: The Destination: Reaching π
sections.content: Combine the concepts: If the exponent 'x' in e^(ix) represents the distance traveled along the arc (in radians), then setting x = π means traveling exactly half the circumference of the unit circle.
sections.example: Digit the Robot walks along the circle track for exactly π distance (3.14159... units). He started at '1', and after half a circle, he is now standing exactly at '-1'. Equation solved: e^(πi) = -1.

sections.title: Summary: The Bridge Between Algebra and Geometry
sections.content: Final synthesis: Euler's identity isn't just a formula; it's the realization that continuous rotation (Group Theory) and exponential growth (Calculus) are two sides of the same coin.
sections.example: A cinematic zoom-out showing the number line, the circle, and the formula e^(πi) + 1 = 0 glowing as a unified symbol of mathematical balance.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Complex Plane as a Map
lecture_lines: Welcome to the complex plane, a 2D number map.
We begin at one on the real axis.
Our guide, Digit, will lead the way.
animations: 1. Fade in a 2D coordinate system with white (#FFFFFF) axes, using [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/digit.svg] for numerical markings, and labels 'Real' and 'Imaginary'.
2. Highlight the horizontal 'Real' axis in blue (#0000FF) and the vertical 'Imaginary' axis in red (#FF0000).
3. Draw a unit circle in white (#FFFFFF) centered at the origin to define the movement path.

storyboard.title: The 'i' Operator: Rotation, Not Just a Number
lecture_lines: A single rotation by i turns us ninety degrees.
This action places us at the imaginary unit i.
Repeating the rotation lands us on negative one.
animations: 1. Show a yellow (#FFFF00) vector from the origin to (1,0) labeled '1' in white (#FFFFFF).
2. Rotate the yellow (#FFFF00) vector 90 degrees counter-clockwise from (1,0) to (0,1).
3. Flash the label 'i' at (0,1) in green (#00FF00) to represent the first transformation.
4. Rotate the yellow (#FFFF00) vector another 90 degrees counter-clockwise to reach (-1,0).
5. Flash the label '-1' at (-1,0) in red (#FF0000) to show the result of two rotations.

storyboard.title: The Group Theory Lens: Symmetry and SO(2)
lecture_lines: All unit rotations form the circular group structure.
Rotation represents a fundamental symmetry in mathematics.
We identify this symmetry group as SO(2).
Numbers on a line map to rotations on the circle.
Adding values translates to compounding these rotations.
animations: 1. Display the text 'Group U(1)' in light blue (#ADD8E6) at the top of the screen above the unit circle.
2. Illustrate two colored arcs (orange #FFA500 and purple #800080) adding together along the circle's circumference.
3. Draw a mapping arrow from a white (#FFFFFF) horizontal line (exponents) to the unit circle (group elements).

storyboard.title: The Exponential Path: Compounding Rotations
lecture_lines: Start with a unit vector pointing towards one.
The imaginary unit i forces a perpendicular growth rate.
Small compounding steps push the vector sideways.
This continuous steering creates a perfect circular path.
We define this as continuous perpendicular growth.
animations: 1. Show a white (#FFFFFF) vector at (1,0) with a small 'Growth' label in cyan (#00FFFF).
2. Add a cyan (#00FFFF) velocity vector at the tip of the main vector, pointing exactly perpendicular (upwards).
3. Animate the vector tip tracing an arc while the cyan (#00FFFF) velocity vector continuously rotates to stay perpendicular.
4. Show a sequence of 15 tiny linear segments in cyan (#00FFFF) approximating the curve of the circle.
5. Smooth the segments into a perfect, solid white (#FFFFFF) unit circle.

storyboard.title: The Destination: Reaching π
lecture_lines: Our robot follows the circle's track.
We measure the distance traveled along this arc.
Walking for pi units takes us half-way around.
We arrive exactly at the value negative one.
This concludes the proof of Euler's famous identity.
animations: 1. Highlight a yellow (#FFFF00) arc growing counter-clockwise from (1,0) along the unit circle.
2. Display a dynamic label 'x = ' next to the arc, with values increasing from 0 to 3.14 (#FFFF00).
3. Stop the arc animation exactly at (-1,0) as the value of x reaches pi.
4. Flash the point (-1,0) in red (#FF0000) and scale up the label '-1'.
5. Fade in the full equation e^(pi*i) = -1 in bold white (#FFFFFF) at the center of the screen.

storyboard.title: Summary: The Bridge Between Algebra and Geometry
lecture_lines: The complex plane unites growth and rotation.
Geometry and algebra merge into a single story.
Euler’s identity remains mathematics' most beautiful balance.
animations: 1. Zoom out the camera to show the unit circle, axes, and the equation e^(pi*i) = -1 in one view.

2. Pulse the labels 'Calculus', 'Geometry', and 'Group Theory' around the central formula in light colors, utilizing the [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bridge.svg] to symbolize the connection between these distinct mathematical fields.
3. Transform the equation into e^(pi*i) + 1 = 0 and make it glow in gold (#FFD700).
